sentences.text:
The PSI of Begur Police Station submitted charge sheet against the accused persons for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 read with section 34 of IPC.
C.C.No.2217/2022 2.

The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-
The case of the prosecution is that CW-1 residing at House No.09, Building No.36/17,
2nd Floor, 5th Cross, Nandishwara Layout, Hongasandra Main Road,
Garvebhavipalya, Bengaluru. CW-1 was knows the accused long back.

From 23.05.2021 to 22.06.2021 the accused No.1 to 4 joined together with common intention falsely reposing confidence upon CW-1 to CW-8 that they were providing Government Job to them and received from CW-1 to CW-8 account to their account for a total amount of Rs.15,18,000/-.
Thereafter, they were neither provide the job nor return their amount and thereby the accused persons have committed the above offences.

After completion of the investigation the PSI of Begur Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused persons for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 read with section 34 of IPC.
3.
Thereafter, the complainant has lodged the complaint in Begur Police station.
In turn they have registered the case under Crime No.0244/2021.
Thereafter, police visited the spot, drew the mahazar, secured in the presence of the C.C.No.2217/2022 accused persons subsequently were enlarged on bail.
Thereafter, on completion of the investigation, I.O. has submitted the charge sheet against the accused persons for the above said offences.
After filing the charge sheet, Court has taken cognizance of the offences against the accused No.1 to 4 and issued summons to them.
4. The accused persons have appeared before the court through their counsel.
Copy of the prosecution papers were furnished under Section 207 of Code of Criminal procedure.

Thereafter,
heard both side.
The accused No.3 and 4 split up.
The charges framed against the accused No.1 and 2 for the offence punishable under sections 406, 420 read with section 34 of IPC.
Read over and explained to the accused No.1 and 2 were pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
After framing of charge the accused No.1 split up.
5. To substantiate the case of the prosecution, the prosecution have examined the eight witnesses as PW-1 to PW- 8 and got marked nine documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-9.
The accused NO 2 did not choose to lead defense evidence.
The C.C.No.2217/2022 statement of the accused 2 under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., is dispensed with.
6. Heard the arguments from both side and perused the deposition and documents.

sentences.text: After hearing the parties and on perusal of records, the following points arose for my consideration.
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that CW-1 was knows the accused long back.

From 23.05.2021 to 22.06.2021 the accused No.1 to 4 joined together with common intention falsely reposing confidence upon CW-1 to CW-8 that they were providing Government Job to them and received from CW-1 to CW-8 account to their account for a total amount of Rs.15,18,000/-.

Thereafter, they were neither provide the job nor return their amount and thereby the accused persons have committed the criminal C.C.No.2217/2022 breach of trust and committed the offence punishable under sections 406 read with section 34 of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the above said date, place and time from 23.05.2021 to 22.06.2021 the accused No.1 to 4 joined together with common intention for the purpose of cheating falsely reposing confidence upon CW-1 to CW-8 that they were providing Government Job to them and received from CW-1 to CW-8 account to their account for a total amount of Rs.15,18,000/-.
Thereafter, they were neither provide the job nor return their amount and committed the offence punishable under sections 420 read with section 34 of IPC?
3. What order?
Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on records.

9. My findings to the above points are as follows:
 POINT No.1 : In the NEGATIVE.
 POINT No.2 : In the NEGATIVE.

POINT No.3 : As per final order, for the  following:-
 REASONS  10.
Point No.1 and 2: These above points are inter- linked with each others and required similar type of appreciation of evidence, Hence, they are taken together for common discussion.

11. In support of its case, the prosecution has examined eight witnesses, the PW-1 is the complainant, PW-2 is the daughter of CW-1, PW-3 is the son-in-law of CW-1, PW-4 is the relative of CW-1 to 4, and 6 to 10, PW-5 is the relative of CW-1 to 5 and PW-7 to 10, PW-6 is the relative of CW-1 to 3 and CW- 5 to 8, PW-7 is the relative of CW-1, 6 and son of CW-8, PW-8 is the relative of M S Basavaraj vs Sadath K.N on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24898884/

The case of the prosecution is that CW-1 residing at House No.09, Building No.36/17, 2nd Floor,
5th Cross, Nandishwara Layout, Hongasandra Main Road, Garvebhavipalya, Bengaluru.
CW-1 was knows the accused long back.

From 23.05.2021 to 22.06.2021 the accused No.1 to 4 joined together with common intention falsely reposing confidence upon CW-1 to CW-8 that they were providing Government Job to them and received from CW-1 to CW-8 account to their account for a total amount of Rs.15,18,000/-.
Thereafter, they were neither provide the job nor return their amount and thereby the accused persons have committed the above offences.

After completion of the investigation the PSI of Begur Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused persons for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 read with section 34 of IPC.
. In the instant case the PW-1 to 8 have turned hostile to the prosecution case and not supported to the prosecution case.
During the course of cross examination by the learned Sr. APP nothing has been elicited from their mouth.
14. In this case, the prosecution has failed to elicit anything favorable to it to prove the allegations against the accused NO2 under sections 406, 420 read with section 34 IPC.
When these being the facts, I am of the opinion that in total the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused NO 2 beyond all reasonable doubt.
In view of the same, this court hold Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
15. Point No.3:
For the reasons stated and finding given to Point No.1 and 2, the following is made.
ORDER The accused No.2 is not found guilty for the offences punishable under section 406, 420 read with section 34 of IPC.
Acting under section 248(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure the accused No.2 is hereby C.C.No.2217/2022 acquitted for the offences punishable under section 406, 420 read with section 34 of IPC.
The bail bonds and surety bonds executed by her stand canceled.
